hooks.text: This ancient stone is the oldest Martian crust ever found.
How did a rosy rock hold four billion years of water?
This eight-hundred-gram rock is Mars' oldest piece of crust.

title: This Sahara Rock is Mars' Oldest Crust
description: The Teghaza 001 meteorite contains 4.1-billion-year-old crystals that prove liquid water once flowed on the Martian surface.

beats.text: This ancient stone is the oldest Martian crust ever found.
beats.visual: Teghaza 001 Martian meteorite specimen on a dark lab background, 2022

beats.text: It's the new record holder, beating the famous Black Beauty meteorite.
beats.visual: The Northwest Africa 7034 Black Beauty meteorite specimen, NASA photo

beats.text: Searchers found the rosy rock in the Sahara back in 2022.
beats.visual: Wide landscape of the Sahara Desert sand dunes in Mali at sunset

beats.text: They used tiny zircon crystals to date it to four billion years old.
beats.visual: Microscopic view of a zircon crystal grain under polarized light

beats.text: This rock is a Rosetta Stone for the Red Planet.
beats.visual: photograph of a planetary scientist analyzing a meteorite in a clean room lab

beats.text: It was blasted off Mars before flinging through deep space.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of an asteroid impact on the surface of ancient Mars

beats.text: Inside, volcanic minerals show liquid water once soaked the surface.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of ancient Mars with oceans and a blue sky

beats.text: It's the ultimate proof that Mars was once a wet world.
beats.visual: The rosy Teghaza 001 meteorite specimen against a starry background

better_than_last: Applied reviewer's requested hook and ensured the loop feels like a natural continuation of the final fact while avoiding forbidden dangling words.
